chunks: Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: Keep the wudu (ablution) consecutive as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: begin with the face, then the two hands, then wipe the head and the two feet. Do not put anything before another thing in a way that opposes what you have been commanded. So if you washed the forearm before the face, then begin with the face and repeat over the forearm; and if you wiped the foot before the head, then wipe over the head before the foot, then repeat over the foot. Begin with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began with.

2- Ibn Abi Jayd al-Qummi informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

One of the two عليهما السلام was asked about a man who began with his hand before his face, and with his feet before his hands. He said: He begins with what Allah began with, and he should repeat what he had done.
3- And by this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام
Regarding a man performing wudu (ablution) who begins with the left before the right, he said: He washes the right and repeats the left.

4- As for what Sa‘d ibn ‘Abdillah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, from ‘Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who performed wudu (ablution) and forgot to wash his left side, and he said:

He washes only his left side and does not repeat any other part of his wudu (ablution). This does not contradict what we have presented regarding sequence, because the meaning of his saying عليه السلام, “He does not repeat anything from his wudu,” is that he does not repeat anything of the limbs that came before washing his left side. Rather, what is obligatory upon him is to complete what comes after this limb. That which indicates this is:

5- What Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman, from سماعة, from Abu Basir, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If you forgot and washed your two forearms before your face, then repeat washing your face, then wash your two forearms after the face. If you began with your left forearm, then repeat over the right, then wash the left. And if you forgot wiping your head until you washed your feet, then wipe your head, then wash your feet.
6- And from him, from ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man forgets to wash his right, then washes his left and wipes his head and his feet, then remembers after that, he washes his right and his left and wipes his head and his feet. But if he only forgot his left, then let him wash the left and not repeat what he had already performed of wudu (ablution). And he said: Follow your wudu, part after part.
7- Al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام

Regarding a man who forgot to wipe his head until he entered into salat (prayer), he said: If there is moisture in his beard enough for what he wipes over his head and his feet, then let him do that and let him pray. He said: And if he forgot anything from the obligatory wudu (ablution), then he must begin with what he forgot and repeat what remains for the completion of the wudu.
8- From him, from Safwan, from Mansur, who said: I asked Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام
about one who forgot to wipe his head until he stood in salat (prayer). He said: He turns away and wipes his head and his feet.
9- As for what Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahbub narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from ‘Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother Musa عليه السلام, he said: I asked him

about a man who is not in a state of wudu (ablution), then rain falls upon him until his head, beard, body, hands, and feet become wet—does that suffice him for wudu? He said: If he washed with it, then that suffices him. This does not contradict what we have already presented, because the correct understanding here is that whoever is struck by rain and then washes his limbs according to the sequence required by wudu, it is permissible for him thereby to make salat (prayer) lawful for himself. But if he does not wash and confines himself merely to the rain falling upon him, that is not sufficient. For that reason he said, when the questioner asked: If he washed with it, then that suffices him.

key_terms.التَّرْتِيبِ: the prescribed sequence of acts in wudu
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, which is wiped in wudu
key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the two feet, wiped in wudu according to the text
key_terms.الْمَطَرُ: rainwater, discussed here regarding its use in wudu
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face, which is washed first in wudu
key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping, especially over the head and feet in wudu

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they perform wudu in the wrong order or forget a part of it?
ai.summary: These narrations establish the legal requirement of sequence in wudu (ablution), requiring the worshipper to begin with the face, then the arms, then the wiping of the head and feet. They also explain how to correct mistakes made through forgetfulness, clarifying when only the omitted limb is to be completed and when later acts must be repeated to preserve the proper order.
